Capacity (MW).note: The Maryland Public Service Commission order of February 2018 says the project's primary power units are two 65 MW heat recovery steam turbines. The state hearing notice says the certificate covers a 130 MW station made of two 65 MW steam turbine units. So each unit is 65 MW.

Turbine/Engine Technology.note: The state documents describe two steam turbine generators running in combined cycle on waste heat from gas turbines that drive the liquefaction compressors. The units in question are the two steam turbines. The gas turbines drive compressors and do not generate power.

Equipment Manufacturer/Model.note: The state order names GE Frame 7EA combustion turbines as the heat source for the steam turbines. I did not find the make of the steam turbines themselves, so this is only partly answered.

Fuel.note: The state order says the Frame 7EA turbines run on natural gas and the steam turbines use their waste heat. The steam units burn no fuel of their own.

Start year.note: A trade article says the Cove Point export terminal began commercial operation in April 2018. It does not name the steam turbines, so I inferred that they began service with the terminal.

Status.note: The terminal began commercial operation in April 2018 and the article from November 2019 reports it loading its 100th ship. No page I found states the steam turbine units' status directly, and the EIA tables do not list them.

Captive industry use.note: The state order says the two steam turbines are the primary power units for the export project, so the power serves the terminal itself.

Owner(s).note: An Oil and Gas Journal article says Berkshire Hathaway Energy completed its purchase of Dominion's 50 percent stake in Cove Point LNG LP, bringing its interest to 75 percent. A Brookfield subsidiary holds the other 25 percent. The article gives the owner as a Berkshire subsidiary, which I wrote as BHE GT&S.

Operator(s).note: The same article says BHE GT&S serves as the general partner and operator of Cove Point.
